title: 24-hour config setting in the widget (not systemwide) does not propagate to items in the "Copy to clipboard" menu
line: The Digital Clock's Copy to Clipboard menu now shows times in the 12 or 24-hour format chosen in the widget's settings.
explanation: The clock's own label builds its time format from the widget's Time display setting, but the Copy to Clipboard menu (ClipboardMenu in the C++ plugin) used the locale's short and long time formats unchanged and never knew about the setting. On a 12-hour locale with the widget set to 24-hour, the menu therefore offered '11:35 AM' while the panel showed 11:35. The widget now passes its setting to the menu, which switches the locale's short and long time formats to the chosen hour cycle (dropping or adding AM/PM, zero-padded hours for forced 24-hour time like the panel) while keeping the rest of each format, such as the time zone name.

commits.message:
applets/digital-clock: Follow the 12/24-hour setting in Copy to Clipboard

The Copy to Clipboard menu used the locale's time formats as they are, so
it offered AM/PM times while the clock was set to 24-hour time, and the
other way round. Pass the setting to the menu and switch both formats.

BUG: 452888

media.caption: Clock set to 24-hour shows 11:35, but every time in Copy to Clipboard has AM/PM (master, sweep tester's shot)
With the fix the same menu lists 16:48, 16:48:00 Central European Standard Time and 24-hour dates, matching the panel

review.text: The cause is right (ClipboardMenu ignores use24hFormat), but the fix adds a 60-line regex rewriter of locale formats in C++ that duplicates, with different rules, what DigitalClock.qml's timeFormatCorrection() already does for the panel label. Two diverging implementations of the same hour-cycle logic are a maintenance burden and the menu can still disagree with the panel (e.g. AM/PM position). Share one implementation instead.
changes: Pass the panel's already-corrected main.timeFormat / main.timeFormatWithSeconds to ClipboardMenu and use them for the time parts (append the time zone separately for the long variant if wanted), or move the hour-cycle conversion into one C++ helper used by both the label and the menu, instead of a second independent rewriter.
